scope: EP77 Key Bridge H001-H121 built-in image generation, exact-ID raw delivery, technical QC, cache provenance verification, and preliminary visual QC only

visual_qc.method: All 11 labelled contact sheets reviewed; selected anomaly candidates were then inspected at original resolution.

findings.H024: 2024-era episode register mismatch and common NEG violation: the tug reads as a steam-era vessel and visible crew bodies appear although the plate has no P flag.
findings.H028: Semantic mismatch: the oversized open-ended cylinder does not read as a voyage data recorder capsule.
findings.H049: Direct order conflict surfaced in pixels: the individual prompt requests a patrol car while the shared NEG forbids patrol cars; output contains the forbidden patrol car.
findings.H087: Owner review required: the requested dawn scene rendered as pronounced golden-hour light, which the shared NEG forbids.
findings.H101: Era and lighting mismatch: the surveyor, coat and instrument read as historical rather than 2024-2026, with pronounced golden-hour light.
findings.H104: Semantic and shared-NEG mismatch: one continuous coastal bridge appears instead of a long line of bridges; the result is an aerial golden-hour view.
findings.H105: Owner review required: blank gantry is correct, but the sunrise is pronounced golden-hour light forbidden by the shared NEG.
findings.H109: Era and lighting mismatch: the port, boats and industrial skyline read as historical; pronounced golden-hour sky conflicts with the shared NEG.
findings.H110: Era mismatch: the aerial working port reads as an early industrial/steamship harbour rather than a 2024-2026 port.
findings.H114: Era/material mismatch: the old masonry pier and timber dolphins do not read as newly installed contemporary protection; golden-hour light is also present.
findings.H116: Era and lighting mismatch: the family car is visibly vintage and the bridge reads historical rather than 2024-2026; golden-hour light is present.
findings.H121: Semantic and shared-NEG mismatch: a full human body appears on a deck requested as empty; the deck is therefore not empty.
